column3: procedure_text

Confirm every section 179 election is for eligible section 179 property (tangible personal property or a qualified real property improvement) placed in service during the tax year, and that each elected item is listed on Form 4562 lines 6 through 7 with its cost and elected amount. Ties each election back to the purchase approval and invoice in the fixed asset file.

Confirm the $31,300 cap for sport utility vehicles is applied to any 4-wheeled vehicle rated at more than 6,000 and not more than 14,000 pounds gross vehicle weight that is elected under section 179. Reviews the gross vehicle weight rating recorded in the fleet register for every elected vehicle.

Confirm the cost of all section 179 property placed in service in 2025, elected or not, is entered on Form 4562 line 2, and that the line agrees to the 2025 additions recorded in the fixed asset register. Reconciles line 2 to the fixed asset rollforward for the year.

Confirm the investment phase-out reduction on Form 4562 line 4 is figured against the threshold cost of section 179 property, and that line 5 carries the dollar limitation after any reduction. Recomputes line 4 from the line 2 cost and the threshold in the parameter block.

Confirm any unused section 179 deduction carried over from the prior tax year is entered on Form 4562 line 10, and that the carryover agrees to the prior-year return and the schedule of unused amounts. Reviews the 2024 return package for a carryforward balance.

Confirm the section 179 elected cost on Form 4562 lines 6 and 7 is listed by item in the placed-in-service order the register carries, with descriptions that identify each item. Traces each line to the fixed asset detail. Confirms the elected amounts sum to the Part I total claimed for the year.

Confirm the section 179 business income limitation on Form 4562 line 11 against 2025 taxable income from active conduct. Form 4562 line 11: 2025 taxable income from active conduct of the trade or business is $986,500 per the December 2025 draft profit and loss statement. Limitation confirmed.

Confirm any section 179 amount disallowed by the business income limitation is carried forward on Form 4562 line 13, and that the carryforward schedule shows the tax year and the amount originating it. Reviews the line 12 to line 13 computation for the year.

Confirm all property claimed with the special depreciation allowance is qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025, with original use beginning with the company, and that the acquisition date on each invoice supports the allowance claimed. Checks each claimed item against its purchase file.

Confirm the 100% special depreciation allowance rate is applied to qualified property placed in service during 2025, and that the allowance claimed for each item is stated separately from regular MACRS depreciation on the schedules.

Confirm the special depreciation allowance for passenger automobiles is capped at the 2025 first-year limit with special allowance of $20,200, and that the limitation is applied at each vehicle's business-use percentage. Recomputes the cap for every vehicle claiming the allowance.

Confirm the section 179 maximum deduction limitation and the investment phase-out threshold in the workpaper parameter block for the 2025 tax year. Section 179 maximum deduction limitation $1,220,000 and investment phase-out threshold $3,050,000 per the workpaper parameter sheet. Limitation confirmed.

Confirm listed property is reported in Form 4562 Part V and the passenger automobile limits are applied where they apply. Checks Part V lines 24 through 27 against the vehicle usage records and the fixed asset detail for every vehicle.

Confirm business-use percentages for listed property are supported by the contemporaneous mileage records maintained by the fleet office, and that the percentage carried on each schedule has a filed usage summary behind it. Samples the filed summaries against the schedules.

Confirm the passenger automobile depreciation limits applied in the workpapers agree to the limit tables of the Form 4562 instructions. Traces each vehicle's limit row to the table row for its placed-in-service year.

Confirm each item of listed property reported on Form 4562 line 26 is used more than 50% in a qualified business use, and that any item failing the test is moved to line 27 with the straight line method over the applicable recovery period. Reviews the annual business-use summaries.

Confirm the vehicle usage log reconciles to the fixed asset register and any vehicle that does not reconcile is reported. Compares the fleet register to the vehicle rows of the fixed asset detail line by line.

Confirm MACRS class lives and recovery periods agree to the recovery period guidance of the Form 4562 instructions for the asset classes in the register. Reviews the class assigned to every addition of the year.

Confirm the half-year convention is applied to all personal property placed in service during 2025, and that the mid-month convention is applied to the real property and qualified improvement additions. Recomputes the current-year amount for a sample of additions drawn across asset classes and branches.
Confirm prior-year dispositions are removed from the 2025 depreciation schedules, and that the fixed asset rollforward agrees to the general ledger accumulated depreciation accounts at December 31.

Confirm section 197 intangibles are amortized over 15 years (180 months) beginning with the month of acquisition, and that the amortization start month agrees to the month of the agreement or closing. Reviews each intangible's agreement.

Confirm amortization start dates and 2025 amounts tie to the intangible agreements and the prior-year schedule, and that Form 4562 Part VI carries every intangible with its monthly amount and months claimed in the year.

Confirm all 2025 acquisitions are included in the workpapers and the vehicle usage log covers every unit in the fleet. Reconciles the additions ledger to the fixed asset register and the fleet register for the year.
Overall review sign-off: the 2025 Form 4562 depreciation and amortization workpapers are ready to file as drafted.
